Source: https://github.com/lioncash/dynarmic
Revision: a41c380246d3d9f9874f0f792d234dc0cc17c180
License: 0BSD (LICENSE.txt), with GPL-3.0-or-later additions identified in source
headers; bundled dependencies retain their own licenses.

Vendored source including bundled dependencies. Built for A64 by nixe-cpu-jit.

Nixe adaptations:
- A64 x64 memory callbacks can abort terminal host failures without retaining
  precise recoverable guest state across every ordinary access. The bridge
  uses Lichii's normal memory policy independently of extended ARM ISA selection;
  callback guards preserve immediate cancellation/failure exit. Recoverable
  precise-memory-abort configurations remain supported by the vendor interface.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64: omit halt checks on forward links in no-cycle mode,
  following Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160, with an additional
  compile-time code-page boundary check to bound unchecked forward chains.
  Backward/indirect exits and page crossings retain checks; no runtime budget
  counter is added. Cycle-counted and single-step paths keep their contracts.
- backend/x64/{a64_emit_x64,emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,block_of_code}:
  reuse adjacent arithmetic NZCV and final check-bit host flags in no-cycle
  mode, following Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Keep committed
  guest flags, carry polarity and conservative immediate/callback boundaries.
  Emission-position proofs never cross blocks; verbose instrumentation and
  cycle-counted terminals retain explicit check-bit storage.
- backend/{code_cache_hash,block_range_information}, backend/x64/{emit_x64,
  a64_emit_x64}, and ARM64-host descriptor owners: mix the full PC/context key
  for robin maps/sets, including incoming references, invalidation and fastmem
  markers. Follows the postmix decision of Lichii's boost flat containers at
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160, using the existing mcl XMRX mixer.
  Standard hashes are unchanged for clients whose containers already mix.
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64: use a cache-line-aligned 2^16-entry, four-way fast
  dispatch table with full tags and FIFO insertion, following Lichii
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Publish after C++ lookup so capacity
  clears cannot discard a just-inserted tag. Retire only exact tags in all ways.
  A64's software return stack has 32 entries; entry lookup, push/pop masks,
  state offsets and invalidation resets derive from the same owning state.
- backend/x64/{a64_emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,emit_x64_memory}: fold
  single-use scalar base+displacement additions into unchecked fastmem operands,
  following Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. The emission marker
  is stored directly on IR instructions instead of a hash index. Preserve full
  callback addresses, inverse/base restoration, store aliases, precise memory
  aborts and deoptimization. Recovery and fault trampolines use the cold region.
- Diagnostic builds only: count generated dispatch hits/misses and RSB hits;
  record disjoint near/cold emitted bytes alongside the existing compilation
  phases. No generated diagnostic instruction or field is present in normal builds.
- backend/x64/{block_of_code,a64_emit_x64,emit_x64_memory}: shared compact
  A64 exit stubs and a separate cold region following Lichii
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Reserve its final-quarter share
  normally, or seven-sixteenths when precise memory-abort recovery enlarges
  every access stub. The total allocation stays unchanged. Preserve reusable inline deferred
  captures, per-transition halt checks, precise fault metadata and epoch ownership.
  Bound both write fronts independently, commit/protect both on Windows and
  describe actual disjoint regions in symbols and disassembly.
- The native bridge assumes valid commercial-software guest addresses and
  omits fastmem-width checks, following Lichii's Auto policy at
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Real arena/page-table sizes,
  page permissions and coherent fault handling are unchanged. Document the
  simplification at the configuration boundary; other native configurations
  retain their bounded fastmem policy.
- backend/x64/{emit_x64,emit_x64_data_processing,a64_emit_x64}: omit redundant
  U32-to-U64 normalization for the verified producer set used by Lichii
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Widening aliases require a GPR;
  partial-width spill slots are normalized before any 64-bit use. A64 enables
  the policy through its owning code buffer; A32 retains normal emission.
- backend/x64/reg_alloc: preserve evicted values in eligible free callee-saved
  GPRs and copy writable live operands into free registers before spilling,
  following Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Precompute the
  ABI/admission spill-candidate mask once; retain direct IR allocation locations
  and scope-local release tracking. A64 options are enabled in the native bridge;
  other frontends retain their policy. Imported algorithm additions retain the
  reference's GPL-3.0-or-later notices.
- backend/block_range_information: append compiled guest extents to a contiguous
  vector and retire intersecting entries on invalidation, following Lichii
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. Keep separate compilation contexts
  and inclusive u32/u64 endpoints, and reuse capacity across cache clears. Use
  the existing invalidation interval set's logarithmic overlap lookup rather
  than scanning every invalidated interval for every recorded block.
  ARM64-host address spaces also clear their A32/A64 extent records through
  the virtual cache-clear boundary, including capacity-triggered resets in
  the base emitter. This closes a lifecycle omission present in the reference;
  x64 already clears its extent owner at both reset boundaries.
- backend/x64/{perf_map,emit_x64,a32_emit_x64_memory,a64_emit_x64_memory,
  block_of_code}: cache PERF_BUILDID_DIR enablement once, and skip friendly-name
  formatting and the process-wide map mutex when disabled. Follows Lichii
  646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160's PerfMapEnabled decision.
  Retain range-scoped symbol ownership as in its JitSymbols interface: Linux
  keeps live entries and rebuilds the perf map only when a cache range retires,
  preserving other JITs and the owner's prelude. New code allocations retire
  prior names in reused host addresses; teardown retains the last map for
  postmortem sampling. Non-Linux symbol operations remain inline
  no-ops; generated guest code and cache invalidation semantics are unchanged.
- Diagnostic builds only (DYNARMIC_JIT_DIAGNOSTICS, selected by the Rust
  performance-counters feature): owner-written per-JIT lookup/compile counters,
  instruction-input fingerprints, phase timings, native mainline/deferred byte
  counts, and distinct capacity/requested/targeted/fastmem invalidation events.
  Follows Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160's per-JIT counter
  ownership; buffered event/epoch analysis is implemented by the native bridge
  and offline tools. Production builds contain no diagnostic fields, counters,
  clocks or callbacks. Instruction fingerprints are not used for cache validity.
- backend/exception_handler{.h,_posix.cpp}: expose cold fault resolution and
  allow nixe to own POSIX signal capture (DYNARMIC_EXTERNAL_FAULT_HANDLER).
- backend/x64/a64_emit_x64.cpp: check halt/budget at linked and indirect/return
  transitions so scheduler preemption and memory transitions remain bounded.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/sys_dc.cpp: end blocks after cache operations;
  nixe applies ownership transitions after dropping its execution lease.
- ir/opt/a64_get_set_elimination_pass.cpp, ir/opt/passes.h and
  both A64 backends: retain setters visible at memory-abort exits
  while still forwarding register values and eliminating redundant accesses.
- interface/A64/config.h, frontend/A64/translate and both A64 backends:
  optionally stop at unknown extension HINTs instead of silently dropping their
  semantics on newer guest CPUs.
- A64 PAuth decoding/translation: simplified unsigned-pointer model matching
  Lichii 646b5d17135a2b2701ccc7a959afd0bbbf2f6160. PAC/AUT/XPAC emit no work;
  PACGA uses masked XOR; authenticated branches and loads use plain addresses.
  The translator retains the GPL-3.0-or-later notice and marks this semantic
  approximation @SIMPLIFICATION and @SPECULATIVE. Selection happens at translation time. Removed
  the superseded process keys, QARMA helper/license, IR opcode, host emitters and
  PAuth-specific execution-address checks in host entry/dispatch/return paths.
  Ordinary code-fetch and memory permission checks remain unchanged.
- frontend/A64/translate/impl/load_store_atomic.cpp: LSE atomic operations
  adapted from Lichii revision 21d62e43caa178aeb04e74585b3aad622b278b84
  (src/dynarmic/src/dynarmic/frontend/A64/translate/impl/load_store_atomic.cpp).
  The file retains its GPL-3.0-or-later notice. CPU feature selection enables
  LSE at translation time; exclusive IR implements CAS/CASP, SWP and atomic ALU
  operations, including acquire/release and retries without partial register
  updates. LDAPR uses the existing limited-order acquire memory operations,
  gated by the RCpc CPU feature. A64CheckMemoryAlignment in both host backends
  faults before a misaligned atomic operation; precise memory exits preserve
  earlier setters.

The native bridge selects Lichii's per-JIT code-cache policy: 512 MiB on x64
except Solaris/NetBSD/DragonFly/OpenBSD; the 128 MiB vendor default remains on
other hosts. Allocation, demand residency, full/targeted invalidation and
per-JIT executable ownership use the existing backend, without code sharing.

The Rust/C ABI integration is in crates/cpu-jit. The generic native fault
capture implementation is shared with the interpreter in cpu-direct-memory.
